CREATE TABLE `attachments`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `path` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `attachable_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `attachable_type` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `created_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `updated_at` TIMESTAMP NULL
);
CREATE TABLE `comments`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `ticket_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `user_id` INT NULL,
    `new_status` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `private` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `body` TEXT NOT NULL,
    `created_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `updated_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY(`user_id`) REFERENCES `users`(`id`), 
  FOREIGN KEY(`ticket_id`) REFERENCES `tickets`(`id`)
);
CREATE TABLE `failed_jobs`(
    `id` BIGINT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `connection` TEXT NOT NULL,
    `queue` TEXT NOT NULL,
    `payload` LONGTEXT NOT NULL,
    `exception` LONGTEXT NOT NULL,
    `failed_at` TIMESTAMP NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE `ideas`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `requester_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `status` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `title` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `repository` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `issue_id` INT NULL,
    `due_date` DATE NULL,
    `body` TEXT NOT NULL,
    `development_effort` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `sales_impact` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `current_impact` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `created_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `updated_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `deleted_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY(`requester_id`) REFERENCES `requesters`(`id`)
);
CREATE TABLE `kpis`(
    `date` DATE NOT NULL,
    `type` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `kpi` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `relation_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `total` INT NOT NULL,
    `count` INT NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY(`date`, `type`, `kpi`, `relation_id`)
);
CREATE TABLE `lead_status_updates`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `new_status` INT NOT NULL,
    `body` TEXT NULL,
    `lead_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `user_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `created_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `updated_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY(`user_id`) REFERENCES `users`(`id`), 
  FOREIGN KEY(`lead_id`) REFERENCES `leads`(`id`)
);
CREATE TABLE `leads`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `email` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `status` INT NOT NULL,
    `team_id` INT NULL,
    `user_id` INT NULL,
    `name` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `body` TEXT NULL,
    `username` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `address` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `city` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `country` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `postal_code` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `company` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `phone` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `created_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `updated_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `deleted_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY(`user_id`) REFERENCES `users`(`id`), 
  FOREIGN KEY(`team_id`) REFERENCES `teams`(`id`)
);
CREATE TABLE `memberships`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `user_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `team_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `admin` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `created_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `updated_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY(`user_id`) REFERENCES `users`(`id`), 
  FOREIGN KEY(`team_id`) REFERENCES `teams`(`id`)
);
CREATE TABLE `merged_tickets`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `ticket_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `merged_ticket_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `created_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `updated_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY(`merged_ticket_id`) REFERENCES `merged_tickets`(`id`), 
  FOREIGN KEY(`ticket_id`) REFERENCES `tickets`(`id`)
);
CREATE TABLE `migrations`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `migration` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `batch` INT NOT NULL
);
CREATE TABLE `password_resets`(
    `email` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `token` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `created_at` TIMESTAMP NULL
);

CREATE TABLE `requesters`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `name` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `email` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `created_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `updated_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `no_reply` TINYINT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE `settings`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `slack_webhook_url` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `default_team_id` INT NULL,
    `created_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `updated_at` TIMESTAMP NULL
);
CREATE TABLE `taggables`(
    `tag_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `taggable_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `taggable_type` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY(`taggable_id`) REFERENCES `leads`(`id`), 
  FOREIGN KEY(`tag_id`) REFERENCES `tags`(`id`), 
  FOREIGN KEY(`taggable_id`) REFERENCES `tickets`(`id`)
);
CREATE TABLE `tags`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `name` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `created_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `updated_at` TIMESTAMP NULL
);
CREATE TABLE `tasks`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `lead_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `user_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `body` TEXT NOT NULL,
    `datetime` DATETIME NULL,
    `completed` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `created_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `updated_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY(`user_id`) REFERENCES `users`(`id`), 
  FOREIGN KEY(`lead_id`) REFERENCES `leads`(`id`)
);
CREATE TABLE `teams`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `name` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `email` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `slack_webhook_url` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `token` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `created_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `updated_at` TIMESTAMP NULL
);
CREATE TABLE `ticket_events`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `ticket_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `user_id` INT NULL,
    `body` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `created_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `updated_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY(`user_id`) REFERENCES `users`(`id`), 
  FOREIGN KEY(`ticket_id`) REFERENCES `tickets`(`id`)
);
CREATE TABLE `ticket_types`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `name` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `color` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `deleted_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `created_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `updated_at` TIMESTAMP NULL
);
CREATE TABLE `tickets`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `title` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `body` TEXT NOT NULL,
    `public_token` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `requester_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `team_id` INT NULL,
    `user_id` INT NULL,
    `status` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `priority` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `level` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `rating` TINYINT NULL,
    `created_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `updated_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `deleted_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `ticket_type_id` INT NULL,
    `subject` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `summary` TEXT NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY(`ticket_type_id`) REFERENCES `ticket_types`(`id`), 
  FOREIGN KEY(`user_id`) REFERENCES `users`(`id`), 
  FOREIGN KEY(`requester_id`) REFERENCES `requesters`(`id`), 
  FOREIGN KEY(`team_id`) REFERENCES `teams`(`id`)
);

CREATE TABLE `user_settings`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `user_id` INT NOT NULL,
    `daily_tasks_notification` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `tickets_signature` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `new_ticket_notification` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `ticket_assigned_notification` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `ticket_updated_notification` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `new_lead_notification` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `lead_assigned_notification` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `new_idea_notification` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `mention_notification` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `ticket_rated_notification` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `created_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `updated_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `escalated_ticket_notification` TINYINT NOT NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY(`user_id`) REFERENCES `users`(`id`)
);
CREATE TABLE `users`(
    `id` INT NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    `name` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `email` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `locale` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `password` VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    `admin` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `assistant` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `remember_token` VARCHAR(255) NULL,
    `created_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `updated_at` TIMESTAMP NULL,
    `can_see_reports` TINYINT NOT NULL,
    `token` VARCHAR(255) NULL
);
gold_question:
1) Background / Context

Handesk is a centralized help desk and lead management application developed by Revo Systems. It is designed to streamline the handling of customer support requests and efficiently manage team leads. The application supports multiple teams and integrates seamlessly with existing projects via a REST API.

2) Objectives

The primary objective of Handesk is to enhance customer support efficiency and lead management by providing a powerful ticketing system. It aims to facilitate communication, issue tracking, reporting, and analytics across multiple teams, allowing for better customer attention and internal team management.

3) Stakeholders & Users

- Primary Users: Customer support teams and lead management teams.
- Administrators: Individuals responsible for overseeing support processes and managing configuration settings.
- Developers: Users interested in leveraging the open-source nature for customization and feature development.

4) Functional Descriptions

- Ticket Management: Centralized ticketing system to manage customer support requests.
- Lead Management: Tools for handling and updating lead statuses, with features to assign leads to teams.
- Multiple Teams Support: Ability to manage and serve multiple teams under one account.
- Email Polling: Automatically retrieve support tickets from an inbox account.
- REST API: Easy-to-use API for integrating Handesk with other projects.
- Issue Tracking: Features to escalate tickets and link with a code issue tracker.
- Reports & Analytics: View and analyze team performance metrics.
- Multilanguage Support: User interface available in multiple languages.

5) Non-Functional Descriptions

- Open Source: Accessible for customization and community-driven enhancements.
- Scalability: Capable of scaling to accommodate growing numbers of tickets and leads.
- Usability: Intuitive interface aimed at enhancing user productivity.
- Security: Secure handling of tickets, leads, and user data.
- Reliability: Ensures consistent performance and uptime for critical customer support operations.
nl_text: The schemabench_0050 database is designed to manage various aspects of a business, including customer interactions, team management, and task assignments. The database consists of 22 tables that work together to store and retrieve data. The attachments table stores files associated with various entities, with each attachment having a unique ID, path, and reference to the entity it belongs to. The comments table contains customer feedback and comments on tickets, with each comment linked to a specific ticket and user. The failed jobs table tracks any errors that occur during the execution of background tasks. The ideas table stores suggestions and ideas submitted by customers, with each idea linked to a requester and having various attributes such as status, title, and due date. The kpis table tracks key performance indicators, with each indicator having a date, type, and relation ID. The lead status updates table stores updates made to customer leads, with each update linked to a lead and user. The leads table contains information about customer leads, including their email, status, and team assignment. The memberships table tracks team membership, with each member linked to a user and team. The merged tickets table stores information about merged tickets, with each merged ticket linked to the original ticket and the merged ticket. The migrations table tracks database migrations, with each migration having a unique ID and batch number. The password resets table stores reset tokens for user passwords. The requesters table contains information about customers who have submitted ideas, with each requester having a unique ID, name, and email. The settings table stores global settings for the application, including the default team ID and Slack webhook URL. The taggables table links tags to leads and tickets, with each taggable item having a unique ID and type. The tags table stores tags used to categorize leads and tickets, with each tag having a unique ID and name. The tasks table contains tasks assigned to users, with each task linked to a lead and user. The teams table stores information about teams, including their name, email, and Slack webhook URL. The ticket events table stores events related to tickets, with each event linked to a ticket and user. The ticket types table stores types of tickets, with each type having a unique ID, name, and color. The tickets table contains information about tickets, including their title, body, and status. The user settings table stores user-specific settings, including notification preferences and signature. The users table contains information about users, including their name, email, and password.
